## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Kilocode connection reset backoff SMALL ~2-3h (core, error-backoff)

- **What**: Kilocode PR #14893 (merged 2026-10-11) moves connection reset retry to normal backoff path. Commit title: "fix(core): retry retryable connection resets through the normal backoff path". When `ErrorBackoff` retry limit reached, provider emitted telemetry event tagged fatal, but `NetworkManager` retried again outside ErrorBackoff, so user saw success after "fatal" event. Double-retry disabled graceful degradation (retry-limit-reached should stop trying, not continue). Fix: (1) `isFatal(error)` now returns true when error is transient (`isRetryable()` true) BUT retry budget exhausted (retried >= maxRetries), (2) NetworkManager checks `isFatal()` and stops instead of retrying, (3) provider marks fatal with `providerData.isFatal = true` in telemetry. Connection resets (`ECONNRESET`) are retryable, so exhausted budget makes them fatal. Single retry path enforces budget. Commit also adds tests for ECONNRESET retry-limit exhaustion tagging fatal.

- **Why**: Alexi has `src/core/error-backoff.ts` (ErrorBackoff class exported L176). Check if `isFatal(error)` considers retry-limit exhaustion (grep for `isFatal` in error-backoff.ts). Kilocode issue: transient errors that exhausted retry budget were retried again by outer layer, violating retry contract. Alexi equivalent: (1) audit `error-backoff.ts` for `isFatal()` logic (likely L100-150), (2) check if `isFatal()` returns true when `isRetryable(error)` true AND `this.retries >= this.maxRetries`, (3) check callers (NetworkManager L250-300, provider layer) respect `isFatal()` and stop retrying, (4) if gap exists, add retry-limit-exhaustion check to `isFatal()` (return true when error is retryable but budget spent), (5) test ECONNRESET exhausts budget -> isFatal true -> no further retry. SMALL ~2-3h: audit error-backoff.ts isFatal logic, add retry-limit-exhaustion check if missing, verify callers stop on isFatal true, test ECONNRESET budget exhaustion.

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/14893 (connection reset backoff), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/error-backoff.ts L176 (ErrorBackoff class)

- **Category**: core (error-backoff, retry logic)

- **Size**: SMALL ~2-3h (audit error-backoff.ts isFatal for retry-limit-exhaustion check, add check if missing, verify callers respect isFatal, test ECONNRESET budget exhaustion stops retry)

#### 2. Kilocode MCP interrupt cleanup SMALL ~3-4h (mcp, process cleanup)

- **What**: Kilocode PR #14809 (merged 2026-10-11) cleans up MCP servers when startup interrupted. Commit title: "fix(cli): clean up MCP servers when their startup is interrupted". When user presses Ctrl+C during MCP server connect (waiting for readiness probe), signal handler ran but MCP server process was not killed, leaving zombie. Fix: (1) MCPManager wraps connect in try/catch, (2) on abort signal during connect, cleanup handler calls `server.disconnect()` + `server.kill()`, (3) process is killed before signal propagates to shell. Commit also adds abort-signal-based cancellation to connect retry loop, so retry aborts immediately on Ctrl+C instead of waiting for next retry.

- **Why**: Alexi has MCP support (`src/mcp/` directory). Check if MCP connect has interrupt cleanup. Grep for MCP server startup in `src/mcp/index.ts` or `src/mcp/manager.ts`. Kilocode issue: Ctrl+C during MCP connect left zombie process. Alexi equivalent: (1) audit MCP manager for server startup code (likely `connectServer` or `startServer` function), (2) check if startup is wrapped in try/catch with abort-signal listener, (3) check if cleanup handler kills server process on abort, (4) if gap exists, wrap connect in try/catch, add abort-signal listener (signal from shutdown handler or Ctrl+C), call `server.disconnect()` + `server.kill()` on abort, (5) test Ctrl+C during MCP connect kills server process (no zombie). SMALL ~3-4h: audit MCP startup for interrupt cleanup, add abort-signal listener + cleanup if missing, test Ctrl+C during connect kills server.

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/14809 (MCP interrupt cleanup), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/mcp/ (MCP manager)

- **Category**: mcp (process cleanup, signal handling)

- **Size**: SMALL ~3-4h (audit MCP startup for interrupt cleanup, add abort-signal listener + process kill on abort if missing, test Ctrl+C during connect)

#### 3. Kilocode terminal compaction failure surfacing REFERENCE-ONLY (tools)

- **What**: Kilocode PR #14651 (merged 2026-10-11) surfaces terminal compaction failures. Commit title: "fix(cli): surface terminal compaction failures". Kilocode has `compact-terminal` tool (compacts tmux/screen panes to save tokens). Tool silently failed when tmux/screen unavailable (command not found, no active session), returned empty result, user saw generic "tool failed" error with no hint why. Fix: (1) detect tmux/screen unavailable (command exit code 1, stderr "command not found" or "no server running"), (2) return explicit error message "tmux not installed, install with apt/brew/..." or "no active tmux session, run inside tmux", (3) user knows what to fix. PR also adds unit tests for error cases.

- **Why**: Alexi has no terminal compaction tool (checked `src/tool/tools/`, no `compact-terminal.ts` or tmux/screen references). Not applicable. REFERENCE-ONLY: if Alexi adds tmux integration (terminal multiplexing, session management), remember to surface tool availability errors (tmux not installed, no active session) instead of generic failures. Kilocode pattern: detect common failure modes (command not found, no server), return actionable error message with install/usage hints.

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/14651 (terminal compaction failure surfacing), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/tool/tools/ (no terminal compaction tool)

- **Category**: N/A (tools, reference-only)

- **Size**: SKIP. Alexi has no terminal compaction tool. Reference for future tmux integration.

#### 4. Kilocode Windows ARM64 error message REFERENCE-ONLY (cli)

- **What**: Kilocode PR #14838 (merged 2026-10-11) improves Windows ARM64 missing-binary error message. Commit title: "fix(cli): improve missing binary error message for Windows ARM64". Kilocode ships platform-specific native binaries (x64, ARM64). When Windows ARM64 user ran CLI without x64 emulation enabled, generic error "binary not found" was unhelpful. Fix: detect Windows ARM64 platform (process.arch === 'arm64', process.platform === 'win32'), return explicit error message "Windows ARM64 not yet supported. Run under x64 emulation (Prism). See docs/windows-arm.md". User knows what to do.

- **Why**: Alexi is Node.js-based, no platform-specific native binaries shipped (pure TypeScript + dependencies). Not applicable. REFERENCE-ONLY: reminder to audit Alexi error messages for clarity. If Alexi adds native dependencies or platform-specific code paths (e.g. filesystem watchers, git bindings), surface platform-specific issues with actionable messages instead of generic "failed" errors. Kilocode pattern: detect platform, return explicit guidance with workaround or docs link.

#### 5. Cline default model selection REFERENCE-ONLY (core, model-selection)

- **What**: Cline PR #14959 (merged 2026-10-11) defaults to first recommended model (Sonnet 5.5 fallback). Commit title: "Default to the first Cline recommended model (Sonnet 5.5 fallback) across CLI, extension, and desktop". Cline hardcoded `claude-sonnet-4.6` as default model across surfaces (CLI, VSCode extension, desktop app). Inconsistent with provider manifest `CLINE_RECOMMENDED_MODELS.recommended[0]` (dynamic list curated per provider). Fix: (1) CLI resolves provider SDK default via `provider.defaultModelId` before falling back to first catalog entry, (2) VSCode extension drops hardcoded `openRouterDefaultModelId`, uses SDK default, (3) desktop app swaps bootstrap fallback (`CLINE_DEFAULT_MODEL_ID`) for provider catalog default when catalog loads, (4) scope behavior to Cline providers only (cline/cline-pass), other providers (ollama, lmstudio) use first catalog entry or placeholder "default". Fallback chain: provider manifest recommended -> provider SDK default -> first catalog entry -> hardcoded `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`. Tests added for both branches.

- **Why**: Alexi has model selection via `src/providers/model-selection.ts` and `getDefaultModel` in `src/providers/index.ts`. Check if default model fallback chain matches Cline pattern (provider manifest -> SDK default -> catalog -> hardcoded). Cline issue: hardcoded default diverged from provider-curated list, inconsistent UX. Alexi equivalent: audit model selection for fallback chain order, verify provider manifest default is preferred over hardcoded fallback, verify CLI/TUI consistent. REFERENCE-ONLY: Cline PR shows infrastructure pattern for provider-driven defaults. Revisit if Alexi users report default model UX issues (unexpected model selected, inconsistent between CLI/TUI, ignores provider manifest).

- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14959 (default model fallback chain), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/providers/model-selection.ts (model selection), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/providers/index.ts (getDefaultModel)

#### 6. Cline connector meta tools REFERENCE-ONLY (core, connectors)

- **What**: Cline PR #14755 (merged 2026-10-11) adds in-chat connector authentication via Composio meta tools. Commit title: "feat(core): in-chat connector authentication via Composio meta tools". Cline beta sessions (signed-in users) can now authenticate third-party connectors (Gmail, Slack, Linear, etc.) mid-chat. Agent asks for Gmail access, user clicks Connect Link, authorizes via OAuth, agent continues with new tool. Implementation: (1) session creates meta-tool session through Cline API connectors proxy, (2) registers Composio meta tools (`COMPOSIO_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS`, `COMPOSIO_WAIT_FOR_CONNECTIONS`, `COMPOSIO_SEARCH_TOOLS`, `COMPOSIO_MULTI_EXECUTE`) with custom descriptions (Composio defaults are generic), (3) proxy supplies `session_id` so agent doesn't need it, (4) agent uses meta tools to generate Connect Link, wait for auth, then use newly connected tools. PR adds telemetry for connector meta-tool usage.

- **Why**: Alexi has no Cline API integration, no Composio connector proxy. Alexi supports MCP servers (local tools) but not cloud connector orchestration. REFERENCE-ONLY: Cline pattern shows agent-driven OAuth flow (agent requests tool -> system generates auth link -> user authorizes -> agent uses tool). If Alexi adds cloud tool integrations (OAuth-gated APIs), consider similar meta-tool pattern (MANAGE_AUTH, WAIT_FOR_AUTH) so agent can request permissions mid-chat. Current Alexi MCP servers are local-only, no OAuth.

- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14755 (connector meta tools), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/mcp/ (Alexi MCP, local-only)

#### 8. Cline reasoning levels Gemini REFERENCE-ONLY (providers)

- **What**: Cline PR #14991 (merged 2026-10-11) adds thinking levels for level-only Gemini models. Commit title: "fix(llms): portable reasoning off for all providers, and thinking levels for level-only Gemini models". Cline added reasoning control (thinking tokens, extended thinking) for Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek. Gemini 2.5 supports `thinkingConfig.thinkingLevel` (0-3 scale) but NOT `thinkingTokenBudget` (token-based control is Claude-only). Cline sent `thinkingTokenBudget` to Gemini (ignored), sent `thinkingLevel` to Claude (rejected). Fix: (1) detect provider type (Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek), (2) Claude gets `thinkingTokenBudget` only, (3) Gemini gets `thinkingLevel` only (0=off, 1=low, 2=medium, 3=high), (4) DeepSeek gets no reasoning config (no support), (5) portable reasoning (auto-convert token budget to level) disabled for all providers (was experimental). PR also cleans up unused reasoning flags.

- **Why**: Alexi has reasoning control in `src/providers/reasoning.ts` and `adaptiveThinking.ts`. Check if Gemini models use `thinkingLevel` vs `thinkingTokenBudget`. Cline issue: wrong reasoning config fields sent to wrong providers. Alexi equivalent: audit reasoning.ts for provider-specific config (Claude uses token budget, Gemini uses level, DeepSeek unsupported), verify Alexi sends correct fields per provider. REFERENCE-ONLY: Cline PR clarifies Gemini reasoning API contract (level 0-3 only, no token budget). Revisit if Alexi users report Gemini reasoning issues or if Alexi adds DeepSeek reasoning.

- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14991 (Gemini thinking levels), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/providers/reasoning.ts (reasoning control), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/providers/adaptiveThinking.ts (adaptive thinking)

- **Category**: N/A (providers, reasoning, reference-only)

- **Size**: SKIP immediate work. REFERENCE - audit reasoning.ts for provider-specific config (Claude token budget vs Gemini level), revisit if Gemini reasoning issues reported.
